topics.caution: The droplets planning to go ask 'ઇન્દ્રદેવ' where and how to fall could be explained either as a literal claim that a rain-god decides the weather, or debunked with a line like 'ખરેખર ઇન્દ્રદેવ જેવું કંઈ નથી' — both misrepresent what the text is doing.
topics.guidance: In the explanation, name ઇન્દ્રદેવ as the traditional Gujarati way of picturing rain in a story — the same kind of make-believe as the droplets themselves talking — and keep the focus on the payload (the twelve named ways rain falls: ફરફર, છાંટા, ફોરાં, કરા, પછેડિયો, નેવાધાર, મોલિયો, ઢેફાંભાંગ, અનરાધાર, અરધિયો, સાંબેલાધાર, હેલી); do not turn ઇન્દ્રદેવ into a theology point or a debunking aside, and keep any real_life_example inside the child's own experience of rain, not a temple or ritual reference.
